  and intent count overflow now destroys the partially allocated AIR program
  before returning an error, keeping the verification layer fail-closed even on
  synthetic or corrupted DIR inputs. AIR owned-name formatting and string
  cloning now also guard `needed + 1` / `strlen + 1` before allocation.
- DAG metadata recording must not publish a partially indexed resolved type.
  `type_checker_resolution_metadata.c` now inserts into the metadata index
  before committing the key/value/owned arrays, and frees owned constructed
  types when capacity or index insertion fails. This keeps
  `materializer_unresolved=0` and `retired_resolver_calls=0` from hiding an
  allocation-failure leak or stale metadata slot. Constructed generic,
  event-handler, and tuple metadata materializers now guard argument-array
  sizing before allocating temporary `Type **` vectors. Metadata index growth
  now checks capacity doubling before multiplication, and stage lookup/domain
  label slicing guards `len + 1` before allocating copied host/slot names.
- DAG metadata index ownership is split out:
  `type_checker_resolution_metadata_index.c` now owns metadata key hashing,
  open-addressed index insertion/rebuild, capacity growth, and entry lookup.
  `type_checker_resolution_metadata.c` is down to 373 LOC and keeps metadata
  lookup/materialization policy; the index owner is 163 LOC. Gates: direct GCC
  probes for both owners, `perf_contract_smoke.sh`,
  `type_resolution_resolver_inventory_smoke.sh`,
  `type_resolution_dag_smoke.sh` source contract,
  `semantic_core_shape_smoke.sh`, and `build_source_inventory_smoke.sh`.
- DAG graph inventory nodes and edges now allocate their copied labels/reasons
  before publishing `node_count` or `edge_count`, and alias diagnostic-name
  growth guards capacity overflow. The declaration graph must fail closed
  rather than silently adding unlabeled graph facts. Immediate cycle checks,
  cycle validation, and topo-order construction now also guard graph-size array
  allocation before materializing visited/path/queue/order state.
- Module normalizer shadow-name storage must commit `count` only after the
  owned name is allocated. `module_shadow_push(...)` now avoids leaving a NULL
  name in the active shadow stack on allocation failure, and namespace/name
  joins guard size overflow before allocation. `module_shadow_contains(...)`
  now rejects null inputs at the helper boundary. Rename-scope entries now use
  the same allocate-before-commit rule for old/new names.
- Parser declaration hints must not advance the active hint count until the
  owned declaration name is available. `parser_register_decl_hint(...)` now
  guards hint array growth and skips count commit on name allocation failure.
- Slot/flow ownership snapshots are part of the static boundary verifier, not
  best-effort bookkeeping. `slot_analyzer.c` now guards parallel task access
  arrays before arena allocation, and `type_checker_flow_resources.c` /
  `type_checker_flow_loops.c` guard snapshot/vector growth before copying
  resource, slot, qubit, and pool state. `type_checker_flow_match_coverage.c`
  now guards variant coverage bitsets before scratch allocation and rejects a
  missing variant-output pointer instead of writing through it.
- CFG source-of-truth residual: direct parallel slot `Read` / `Write` /
  `Release` conflicts now flow through CFG resource snapshots. Slot operations
  mark `slot_flow_access_mask`, snapshots preserve `access_masks`, and
  `resource_snapshot_has_parallel_conflict` /
  `resource_snapshot_has_parallel_race_risk` emit
  `PGY_SEM_PARALLEL_SLOT_CONFLICT` / `PGY_SEM_PARALLEL_SLOT_RACE_RISK` from
  the CFG task-boundary join. `scope_release_slot(...)` now marks
  `PGY_SLOT_FLOW_ACCESS_RELEASE` itself, so release-like helpers cannot bypass
  the CFG access fact. `slot_analyzer.c` remains only as an explicitly
  named pre-CFG compatibility seam for conservative escape/helper provenance
  diagnostics, not the beta-final source of truth. The analyzer now propagates
  failed child analysis instead of silently continuing after an internal
  failure, and `semantic_analyze()` now converts analyzer failure/allocation
  failure into a hard semantic diagnostic rather than treating the slot pass as
  optional.
- CFG resource snapshots now carry an explicit `valid` bit. Snapshot
  allocation/overflow failure can no longer look like "no tracked resources":
  defer, parallel, branch, match, for-loop, and while-loop analysis report a
  semantic error when snapshot creation or merge fails, keeping the CFG
  ownership lattice fail-closed.
- CFG/body safety residual is now named instead of hidden behind the main Slot
  analyzer API. Parameter escape summaries used by call/ownership diagnostics
  consume `slot_analyze_legacy_ast_param_summary_in_program(...)` from
  `slot_summary.h`, and those consumers no longer include the full
  `slot_analyzer.h` surface. The legacy implementation entry is no longer a
  public API, and LLVM local slot sinking must also call the explicit legacy
  seam while the MIR/CFG replacement fact is not available. This does not
  finish the CFG migration; it makes the remaining AST-walking compatibility
  seam explicit and smoke-gated so it can be retired behind CFG/MIR body facts
  without another A/B/A refactor loop. Gate: `cfg-body-dataflow-test-smoke`.
- Semantic diagnostic emission is also source-of-truth state. Diagnostic array
  growth now handles zero-capacity contexts and element-size overflow before
  reallocating, so OOM/overflow cannot leave diagnostics half-published or
  silently wrap the diagnostic inventory. Gate used: local `test_semantic.exe`
  build and run, `2502 passed, 0 failed`.
- C backend output buffers must not use wrapped length arithmetic as an
  implicit codegen contract. `codebuf_write(...)` and `codebuf_write_raw(...)`
  now share a fail-closed reserve helper that checks `len + payload + NUL` and
  capacity doubling before `realloc`. Gate used: local `transpiler_context.o`
  compile through the `pgy.exe` build graph; full link exceeded the local
  timeout before completion.
- LLVM backend dynamic-array helper macros must follow the same policy:
  `PGY_DYNARR_ENSURE*` now rejects negative capacity, capacity-doubling
  overflow, and element-size multiplication overflow before `realloc`, so
  shared backend helper growth cannot wrap `int` capacity arithmetic.
- The common arena allocator is also part of the allocation source-of-truth:
  block header sizing, pointer-aligned allocation size, active-block
  `used + n`, and total-allocation accounting now guard overflow before
  committing arena state. Gate used: local `arena.o` compile.
- Type environment mutation helpers must honor their null-guard contract before
  reading counters. `type_env_add_variable(...)` and `type_env_add_type(...)`
  now check `env` before accessing `var_count` / `type_count`.
- Type constructors must fail closed instead of producing null-name type
  objects. Primitive/generic/constructed/function/tuple constructors now guard
  owned-name allocation, null inputs, argument-array sizing, and rendered type
  name length overflow before committing type metadata. Singleton cleanup is
  now null-safe so partial initialization failure cannot crash cleanup.
- Import/path utility helpers must be null-safe at their public boundary and
  guard rendered path length before allocation. `path_dirname_dup(...)`,
  `path_join_dup(...)`, and Windows `.exe` resolution now fail closed on null
  input or oversized path construction.
- AIR evidence nodes must allocate provenance before committing the evidence
  slot. `air_append_evidence_node_ex(...)` now snapshots the owned-name
  inventory, rolls back partial provenance names on allocation failure, and
  only increments `evidence_count` after the node is fully populated.
- The slot model removes the Rust-style lifetime annotation tax from the self-host path.
- Missing for full self-host: stable module/package resolver, richer stdlib, debugger/bootstrap story, and Stable C escape hatch policy.
- DWARF/CodeView debug information is a post-BETA but pre-self-host requirement:
  current `pgy debug` is an AST-walking source debugger only. Before serious
  Pergyra-debug-Pergyra work, LLVM DIBuilder Phase 1 must wire
  compile-unit/file/line/function/variable-scope metadata and prove it through
  a GDB/LLDB smoke. Do not market the current debugger as binary debugging.
- Generic monomorphization explosion is a measurement risk, not a beta blocker:
  after dogfood, record compile time and binary size for generic-heavy examples
  before considering dictionary passing or selective monomorphization.
- WebGL dogfood is not core language surface. The beta path is `Pergyra -> C backend --emit-c -> optional Emscripten/WebGL bridge`; it validates host bridge viability only. `pgy.render.webgl`, richer render APIs, native LLVM wasm, and GPU/Spray work stay module ecosystem tracks after beta closure.
- Self-hosted compiler layout must use feature/module folders, not C-style
  filename namespaces. The current C compiler can survive with long filenames,
  include-order seams, and Makefile inventory, but the Pergyra compiler must
  expose architecture through module paths and namespaces.
- Runtime hot-path containers must still fail closed on impossible shape, even
  when the normal dogfood sizes are small. Raw exported lists, queues, sets,
  and maps now guard `capacity * 2`, `capacity * elem_size`/`value_size`, and
  the current `uint32_t` hash-index ceiling where hashing still uses 32-bit
  slots before allocation/reindexing. Gate used: local
  `runtime/pgy_runtime_lib.o` compile. `HashMap<String,String>` inline runtime
  growth now applies the same capacity and `uint32_t` hash-index ceiling guard;
  `List<T>`, `List<Int>`, `List<String>`, `Queue<T>`, `Queue<Int>`,
  `Queue<String>`, `Set<String>`, and generic `Set<T>` inline growth now share
  the same checked capacity policy. Generic `HashMap<String,T>` macro growth
  now uses the same checked policy before allocating key/value/occupied arrays,
  and its panic-tail `get` path returns a zero value to avoid generated
  non-void fallthrough warnings. The concrete builtin `HashMap<String,Int>`
  storage path now mirrors that growth and panic-tail policy.
  Gate used: local `pgy_runtime.h` include smoke compiles for
  map/list/queue/set/hashmap paths.
- Runtime intent observability string/subject storage now uses explicit
  `SIZE_MAX` checks before `strlen + 1`, trace append growth, and subject-copy
  array allocation. This keeps the trace/history registry from depending on
  wrapped host arithmetic in malformed or extreme instrumentation paths.
  The active-intent index table is now also guarded as a power-of-two hash-mask
  table in both inline and exported runtime paths, so future table-size edits
  cannot silently break open addressing. Gate used: local
  `runtime/pgy_runtime_lib.o` compile and
  `runtime-intent-observability-contract-test-smoke`.
- Party runtime allocation is now closer to the same fail-closed policy:
  `GenerateFiberMap`, role query result growth, fiber stats index/stats growth,
  and dispatch thread/result array allocation now guard count/element-size
  overflow before allocating. Fiber stats lookup now falls back to the linear
  stats array on hash-index empty-slot misses, so an index insertion failure
  cannot create duplicate role stats on later updates. Gate used: local
  `party_runtime.o`, `party_runtime_stats.o`, and `party_runtime_dispatch.o`
  compiles plus `perf_contract_smoke.sh`.
- Parallel runtime allocation now uses the same count/element-size guard for
  worker pools and parallel block handle/argument arrays, including the
  blocking pool path. Gate used: local `pgy_runtime.h` parallel include smoke
  compile.
- Channel runtime allocation now rejects buffer-capacity multiplication
  overflow before `calloc` for generated generic channels, SPSC channels, and
  the exported `Int` / `String` channel ABI shims. This keeps channel
  initialization fail-closed instead of depending on wrapped allocation sizes.
  SPSC destroy/close/send/recv/space/closed public boundaries now also reject
  null or uninitialized channels instead of dereferencing them after a failed
  init. Gate used: local `pgy_runtime.h` channel include smoke compile and
  `runtime/pgy_runtime_lib.o` compile.
- Async runtime allocation and platform seams are being tightened with the
  same rule. `AsyncScope` fiber-vector growth, scheduler worker-array
  allocation, and async error string cloning now guard overflow; scheduler I/O
  worker and epoll cleanup are explicitly POSIX-only so Windows object compile
  does not see `ioWorker`/`epollFd`/`close`. Gate used: local `async_scope.o`
  and `scheduler.o` compiles.
- Preferred self-host module layout:
  `compiler.frontend.{lexer,parser,ast}`,
  `compiler.semantic.{dag,ownership,effects,intent,zone}`,
  `compiler.ir.{hir,dir,rir,air,mir}`,
  `compiler.backend.{c,llvm,wasm_bridge}`,
  `compiler.runtime_contract.{slot,pin,frontier}`, and
  `compiler.tooling.{fmt,lsp,diagnostics}`.
- Self-host split policy: feature folder first, responsibility owner second.
  `_helpers`-style modules are forbidden unless they are truly cross-feature
  utilities. The self-hosted codebase has Pergyra modules/namespaces, so it
  must not copy the C-era habit of hiding ownership behind helper filenames.
- Current C directory reshuffle is not a beta blocker. Large-scale folder
  recovery belongs to the post-beta self-host path, where Pergyra modules and
  namespaces become the architecture contract.
- 2026-05-11 LLVM intent dispatch-context follow-up:
  non-MIR LLVM intent step context now materializes default dispatch aliases
  from `who` at the context boundary, matching the C backend shape. The LLVM
  intent body emitter no longer reopens `step->data.intent_step.who_names[j]`
  as a local fallback; it consumes `LLVMIntentStepContext` aliases. Gate:
  `mir-declaration-inventory-test-smoke`.
- 2026-05-11 AIR strict-evidence environment parity follow-up:
  `PGY_AIR_STRICT_EVIDENCE` now accepts the same practical false spellings as
  other driver/toolchain toggles (`0`, `false`, `FALSE`, `off`, `OFF`, `no`,
  `NO`) while keeping strict evidence enabled by default. Gate:
  `air-drift-test-smoke`.
- 2026-05-11 AIR evidence owner split follow-up:
  boundary summary-shape validation moved out of the first-class
  `AIREvidenceNode` inventory validator into
  `src/compiler/air_validate_boundary_summary.c`. The main evidence inventory
  owner is now back down to 504 LOC and only owns authoritative evidence lookup,
  global/boundary evidence counters, duplicate detection, and inventory shape
  validation. Gates: targeted object builds for both owners, `test-air`
  (99/0), `air-drift-test-smoke`, `build-source-inventory-test-smoke`, and
  `test-inc-size-test-smoke`.
- 2026-05-11 environment flag parser follow-up:
  AIR strict-evidence toggles and compiler toolchain toggles now share
  `src/common/env_flags.c` instead of carrying independent `0/false/off/no`
  spelling chains. This keeps future CI/tooling flags from drifting on Windows
  or Git Bash spelling conventions. Gates: targeted object builds for
  `env_flags.o`, `air.o`, and `compiler_toolchain.o`, plus
  `air-drift-test-smoke` and `perf-contract-test-smoke`.
- 2026-05-11 backend builtin type registry follow-up:
  `Input`, `Concat`, and `StringConcat` now live in the backend builtin type
  table instead of LLVM call inference carrying a private string-return
  strcmp chain. This keeps C/LLVM type facts on the shared registry path and
  removes one local codegen-only source of truth. Gates: targeted object builds
  for `transpiler_builtin_type_table.o` and `llvm_stmt_type_infer.o`, plus
  `perf-contract-test-smoke`.
- 2026-05-11 LLVM number literal type parity follow-up:
  LLVM expression type inference now mirrors `llvm_emit_number(...)` for
  numeric literals: `1L` and large integral literals infer `i64`, fractional
  literals infer `f64`, and only in-range integral literals infer `i32`. This
  removes another quiet `AST_NUMBER -> i32` assumption from initializer/local
  type selection. Gates: targeted `llvm_stmt_type_infer.o` build and
  `perf-contract-test-smoke`.
- 2026-05-11 C/LLVM numeric let parity follow-up:
  C backend unannotated `let` emission now routes numeric initializer typing
  through `infer_expression_type_name(...)` and the ctx-aware C-type requirement
  path instead of hardcoding `AST_NUMBER` to `int32_t`. This keeps `Long` and
  fractional numeric literals aligned with the LLVM inference/emission path.
  Gates: targeted `transpiler.o` build and `perf-contract-test-smoke`.
- 2026-05-11 C/LLVM arithmetic promotion parity follow-up:
  C backend expression type inference and LLVM expression type inference now
  both promote numeric binary operations through a shared precedence
  (`Double`/`f64`, `Float`/`f32`, `Long`/`i64`, then `Int`/`i32`) instead of
  treating numeric `+` as always `Int`/`i32`. String `+` still stays the string
  concatenation path. Gates: targeted `transpiler.o` and
  `llvm_stmt_type_infer.o` builds, plus `perf-contract-test-smoke`.
- 2026-05-11 LLVM type-inference owner margin follow-up:
  the new LLVM numeric promotion helper moved into
  `llvm_stmt_type_infer_helpers.c`, and visible-function lookup moved there
  as well, keeping `llvm_stmt_type_infer.c` at 546 LOC instead of sitting on
  the 600 LOC boundary. This follows the split-by-responsibility rule: shared
  inference helpers live in the helper owner, while
  `llvm_stmt_type_infer.c` stays focused on expression dispatch. Gates:
  targeted object builds for both owners, `perf-contract-test-smoke`, and
  `test-inc-size-test-smoke`.
- 2026-05-11 LLVM declared call-result type follow-up:
  LLVM expression type inference now checks the active declaration inventory
  return type before falling back to builtin/collection/domain special cases
  and final poison `i32`. This narrows the remaining call-result fact gap
  without reopening broad AST traversal: the lookup goes through
  `llvm_stmt_find_function_decl_by_name(...)`, which is backed by the active
  LLVM declaration inventory. Gates: targeted object builds for
  `llvm_stmt_type_infer.o` and `llvm_stmt_type_infer_helpers.o`, plus
  `perf-contract-test-smoke` and `test-inc-size-test-smoke`.
- 2026-05-11 LLVM binary fallback tightening:
  unsupported binary operators in LLVM expression type inference no longer
  silently return poison `i32`; the recognized boolean, string, and numeric
  operators still infer concrete types, while any unexpected binary operator
  now reports a concrete-type diagnostic. Gate: `perf-contract-test-smoke`.
- 2026-05-11 LLVM channel receive expected-type follow-up:
  `AST_CHANNEL_RECV` type inference now consumes the enclosing expected value
  type when channel metadata is not yet registered, instead of defaulting
  directly to poison `i32`. Registered channel locals with missing
  `Channel<T>` metadata still fail closed with the existing diagnostic, so
  this only covers the MIR/select temporary allocation seam where a concrete
  let/return type is already available. Gates: targeted
  `llvm_stmt_type_infer.o` build and `perf-contract-test-smoke`.
- 2026-05-11 LLVM call expected-type fallback tightening:
  unknown/domain helper calls now also consume a concrete enclosing
  `expected_type_name` before falling back to poison `i32`. This avoids
  inventing `i32` for typed `let`/`return` contexts while preserving the
  later expression-emission registry diagnostic if the helper function itself
  is missing. Gate: `perf-contract-test-smoke`.
- 2026-05-11 LLVM array element expected-type follow-up:
  `llvm_stmt_resolve_array_elem_type(...)` now derives the element type from
  enclosing `Array<T>` / `Slice<T>` expected type context before using its
  legacy `i32` recovery. This reduces another local fallback for empty arrays,
  slices, and element-sensitive calls where the source binding already carries
  a concrete annotation. Gates: targeted `llvm_stmt_type_infer.o` build and
  `perf-contract-test-smoke`.
- 2026-05-10 AIR/DAG tightening:
  `AIR_BOUNDARY_WORLD` now classifies as `AIR_SYNC_ASYNC` in the shared
  boundary classifier, matching the validator and handoff model instead of
  silently disagreeing with AIR sync-shape validation. `air-drift-test-smoke`
  gates the contract in both Python and literal-fallback modes. DAG metadata
  index growth now avoids `next_count * 2` / capacity-doubling overflow and
  fails closed on impossible table sizes. Gates used: targeted `gcc
  -fsyntax-only`, `air-drift-test-smoke`, `intent-compression-contract-smoke`,
  `air-json-schema-test-smoke` source/schema fallback, `cfg-body-dataflow`
  source fallback, and `type-resolution-resolver-inventory-smoke`. The full
  DAG execution smoke still requires `SEMANTIC_TEST_BIN` in this local shell.
- 2026-05-10 CFG/MIR source-shape accessor follow-up:
  MIR dump/lifecycle now consumes instruction/block source-shape accessors
  instead of reopening raw `source_ast_type` / `source_line` fields. The
  source-shape owner and MIR construction owner remain the only intended raw
  field users, and `cfg-body-dataflow-smoke` gates this boundary for
  `mir_lifecycle.c`, `mir_stmt_population.c`, `mir_dce.c`, and LLVM MIR block
  emission.
- 2026-05-10 backend MIR source-payload accessor follow-up:
  C and LLVM MIR emitters no longer read `inst->ast` directly. They consume
  `mir_instruction_source_payload(...)`, keeping compatibility AST payload
  access behind the MIR source-shape owner while backend semantics continue to
  consume named MIR facts. `cfg-body-dataflow-smoke` now rejects raw
  instruction AST payload reads under `src/codegen`.
- 2026-05-10 compiler MIR source-payload accessor follow-up:
  MIR DCE, fact validators, and SSA rename no longer reopen `inst->ast`
  directly. They consume `mir_instruction_source_payload(...)`, leaving raw
  instruction AST payload access only in MIR construction/population and the
  MIR source-shape owner. `cfg-body-dataflow-smoke` now rejects raw payload
  reads in compiler consumers outside that allowlist, and `perf-contract-smoke`
  now tracks the accessor-based backend/compiler contract instead of stale
  `inst->ast` literals.
- 2026-05-10 MIR population source-match follow-up:
  MIR statement population now uses
  `mir_instruction_source_matches_ast_node(...)` when matching resource ops
  back to source statements. Population may still attach compatibility source
  payloads, but source-shape matching stays behind the named MIR source-shape
  predicate instead of direct `inst->ast == stmt` checks. The raw payload smoke
  allowlist no longer includes `mir_stmt_population.c`.
- 2026-05-10 AIR RIR propagation counter/fact invariant:
  AIR validation now requires collector-produced RIR propagation summary
  counters to match authoritative global evidence fact counts whenever RIR
  input is present. This prevents `rir_*_propagation_evidence_count` from
  becoming a second source of truth beside `AIR_EVIDENCE_RIR_*_PROPAGATION`
  nodes for both effect and relation propagation. The regression lives in
  `test_air_rir_propagation_part_j.cases.h`, and `air-drift-test-smoke`
  gates both the diagnostic and the test entry.
- 2026-05-10 AIR global evidence counting split:
  AIR evidence presence now uses `air_global_evidence_node_count(...)`, while
  propagation completeness continues to use `air_global_evidence_fact_count(...)`.
  This keeps node-presence checks separate from fact-cardinality checks and
  avoids reintroducing counter/fact semantic drift.
- 2026-05-10 AIR/MIR source-shape link inventory follow-up:
  `AIR_CORE_OBJECTS` now links `mir_source_shape.o` plus the MIR statement and
  CFG-control classification owners it depends on because AIR MIR evidence
  consumes MIR source-shape predicates for CFG terminator/select-receive
  evidence. This keeps the Makefile inventory aligned with the source-of-truth
  boundary instead of relying on incidental MIR test link sets.
- 2026-05-10 AIR global boundary-evidence drift validation follow-up:
  `AIR_DRIFT_BOUNDARY_EVIDENCE_MISSING` is now allowed as a global drift kind
  when strict AIR reports missing global evidence such as observability schema,
  runtime frontier policy, or MIR CFG terminator evidence. This keeps repeated
  `air_check_drift` calls valid while still rejecting malformed indexed drift
  inventory.
- 2026-05-10 DAG ability-contract seam follow-up:
  ability references are contract/capability coordinates, not ordinary value
  type materialization targets. `resolve_required_ability_decl(...)` now records
  the DAG dependency without forcing `Ability<T>` through the generic type
  materializer, while role require-field validation substitutes simple ability
  generic parameters from effective/default arguments before consulting cached
  metadata. This restored generic ability defaults and default-exported generic
  ability contracts while keeping `retired_resolver_calls=0`,
  `metadata_dead_ends=0`, and `materializer_fallbacks=0`.
- 2026-05-10 DAG placeholder metadata-first follow-up:
  Top-level program placeholders now use `semantic_type_resolution_lookup_metadata_type_ref(...)`
  through `program_lookup_dag_type_ref_or_unknown(...)` instead of the last
  annotation-only lookup seam. `type-resolution-resolver-inventory-smoke` now
  gates `annotation-only reads=0 cap=0`; stable placeholders may read DAG
  metadata but must not locally materialize or re-enter the retired recursive
  resolver.
- 2026-05-10 DAG annotation-or-unknown retirement follow-up:
  removed the dead `semantic_type_resolution_lookup_annotation_or_unknown(...)`
  declaration and implementation after all call sites moved to metadata-first
  type-ref helpers. The resolver inventory smoke now treats that symbol as
  fully retired instead of allowing it inside private metadata owners.
- 2026-05-11 DAG ability owner seam consolidation follow-up:
  ability declaration signatures, ability `fields` requirements, and ability
  where-bound validation now share `ability_resolve_type_ref(...)` instead of
  each owner calling the metadata materializer seam directly. The resolver
  inventory smoke now keeps fallback seams, annotation-only reads, nullable
  annotation reads, and materializing type-ref helper refs at `0`.
- 2026-05-11 DAG projection/role/intent/host/event/world/expression owner seam
  consolidation follow-up:
  projection builtin target-field validation, domain-query projection source
  lookup, and recursive projection path lookup now share
  `projection_resolve_type_ref(...)`. This keeps projection diagnostics owned by
  projection validators while the broader declaration/domain consumers moved
  toward metadata-only owner seams. The intermediate cap staircase
  (`30/27/24/21/18/15/12/9/6`) has converged to
  `type-ref helper refs=0 cap=0`; historical per-owner cap notes are superseded
  by the resolver-inventory smoke.
- 2026-05-13 DAG unresolved-family naming follow-up:
  `SemanticContext` dead-end family counters use
  `type_resolution_metadata_unresolved_*` names internally. The public stats
  labels remain `metadata-unresolved-*`, and the old `materializer_fallbacks`
  mirror has since been removed. The resolver-inventory smoke rejects
  reintroducing `type_resolution_metadata_fallback_*` fields or fallback-era
  mirror counters under `src/semantic`, so DAG dead-end accounting cannot drift
  back into fallback-era naming.
- 2026-05-13 CFG predecessor inventory shape follow-up:
  HIR and MIR validators now both reject predecessor counts that exceed their
  recorded predecessor capacity. This keeps CFG predecessor inventory as a
  checked source-of-truth fact before PHI, liveness, cleanup, and backend
  consumers read it. Gates: targeted `hir_validate.c` /
  `mir_cfg_contract_edges.c` object builds, `src/test_hir.c` /
  `src/test_mir.c` syntax probes, and `cfg-body-dataflow-test-smoke`.
- 2026-05-11 CFG/MIR pin cleanup root regression follow-up:
  added an executable MIR regression for the existing invariant that any
  reachable pin region must have a cleanup root, not just a matching
  `pin-unpin-cleanup-edge` fact. This fills the gap where
  `cfg_body_dataflow_smoke.sh` required the named regression but the MIR suite
  did not yet instantiate it. Gates: `cfg_body_dataflow_smoke.sh`,
  `gcc -fsyntax-only src/test_mir.c`.
- 2026-05-11 AIR pin cleanup root consumer follow-up:
  added a strict AIR regression for a reachable pin boundary whose MIR pin block
  carries a pin cleanup edge fact but no registered cleanup root. AIR must not
  collect MIR pin cleanup evidence for that shape, and strict verification must
  report missing pin cleanup evidence. This keeps AIR consuming MIR cleanup-root
  truth instead of accepting local edge facts without a root. Gates:
  `air_drift_smoke.sh`, `gcc -fsyntax-only src/test_air.c`, `test-air`
  (`105/0`).
- 2026-05-11 AIR consumer coverage status refresh:
  `docs/104_air_compiler_architecture.md` no longer lists RIR effect/relation
  propagation as missing AIR 1.0 evidence coverage. Those paths now have global

  runtime frontier scheduler coverage.
- 2026-05-11 AIR MIR summary-counter closure:
  strict AIR now rejects MIR cleanup and select-receive summary counters unless
  matching global `AIREvidenceNode` entries exist. MIR terminator counter-only
  rejection remains covered by the same rule, so cleanup, terminator, and
  select-receive evidence all share the same source-of-truth contract:

  AIR validation also rejects MIR global evidence node-count drift when MIR
  evidence nodes are present, while preserving counter-only cases as verifier

  `test-air` (`108/0`), `test_inc_size_smoke.sh`, and
  `build_source_inventory_smoke.sh`.
- 2026-05-11 AIR summary-counter owner split:
  MIR/RIR summary-counter-to-`AIREvidenceNode` consistency checks moved out of
  `air_validate_evidence.c` into `air_validate_summary_counters.c`. Evidence
  inventory shape remains in the evidence owner, while compatibility telemetry
  counter matching has its own owner. This keeps `air_validate_evidence.c` at
  510 LOC after the stricter AIR evidence work and avoids another mechanical
  `_helpers` split.
- 2026-05-11 AIR verification provenance owner split:
  authority/provenance diagnostic string formatting moved from `air_verify.c`
  into `air_verify_provenance.c`. The verifier now owns drift decisions while
  the new owner owns `source_provenance`, `who_provenance`, and authority-name
  rendering. `air_verify.c` drops to 498 LOC and the AIR drift smoke now gates
  the new owner explicitly.
- 2026-05-11 owner-size gate repair:
  `parser_expr.c` moved call-argument growth/prepend/append ownership to
  `parser_expr_call_args.c`, keeping expression parsing below the 600 LOC owner
  cap without adding a generic `_helpers` owner. Oversized AIR/MIR/transpile
  test case headers were split at function or local include boundaries:
  `test_air_boundary_part_e.cases.h`, `test_mir_lowering_part_e.cases.h`, and
  `test_transpile_stdlib_part_b.cases.h`. Gates:
  `test_inc_size_smoke.sh`, `build_source_inventory_smoke.sh`, targeted
  `gcc -fsyntax-only` for parser/test owners.
- 2026-05-10 AIR DAG evidence strictness follow-up:
  AIR global DAG evidence now rejects non-zero `fallback_count`, matching the
  DAG source-of-truth rule that graph-backed type evidence must not carry
  retired recursive resolver fallback facts. `test_air` includes an explicit
  fallback-evidence negative case, and `air-drift-test-smoke` source-gates the
  diagnostic string. Gates used: targeted `gcc -fsyntax-only`,
  `air-drift-test-smoke`, and `git diff --check`.
- 2026-05-10 AIR global counter-only evidence follow-up:
  strict AIR now treats MIR/DAG summary counters as observability only. MIR
  terminator, DAG metadata/generic/ability, and RIR effect/relation
  propagation counters no longer satisfy strict verification unless the
  matching `AIREvidenceNode` is present. This closes another source-of-truth
  seam where legacy counters could appear to prove body/DAG/runtime
  propagation facts without graph evidence. Gates used: targeted
  `gcc -fsyntax-only` and `air-drift-test-smoke`.
- 2026-05-10 AIR backend non-consumption gate follow-up:
  `air-drift-smoke` now checks both codegen `.c` and `.h` files for direct
  `air.h` / `AIRProgram` / `air_synthesize` consumption. Codegen may mention
  AIR in comments that explain boundary ownership, but it must not consume AIR
  structures or synthesis APIs; AIR remains a verification-only layer.
- 2026-05-10 AIR MIR evidence provenance follow-up:
  AIR MIR evidence collection now fails closed when a routine has MIR evidence
  facts but no routine name or owner provenance. This prevents anonymous MIR
  evidence nodes from being appended and only later rejected by generic AIR
  evidence validation. `air-drift-smoke` source-gates the collector diagnostic
  and regression case.
- 2026-05-10 AIR RIR evidence provenance follow-up:
  AIR RIR evidence collection now fails closed when a scope has effect/relation
  propagation or boundary evidence but no scope name or owner provenance. This
  keeps RIR propagation evidence from becoming anonymous global facts and
  mirrors the MIR evidence provenance rule. `air-drift-smoke` source-gates the
  diagnostic and regression case.
- 2026-05-10 CFG-owned terminal fallback follow-up:
  MIR CFG contract validation now rejects CFG-owned control fallback STMTs in
  every reachable CFG-backed block, not only branch blocks with true/false
  successors. This closes the terminal-return edge where a CFG-backed routine
  could carry a residual `return`/control AST statement without being caught by
  the source-of-truth validator. Gate used: targeted `gcc -fsyntax-only`.
- 2026-05-10 DAG dead-end mirror naming follow-up:
  Historical note: this step temporarily kept
  `type_resolution_metadata_materializer_fallbacks` as a compatibility stats
  mirror. That mirror has since been removed; the current source of truth is
  `type_resolution_metadata_dead_ends`, and resolver-inventory smoke rejects
  reintroduced materializer fallback mirrors.
- 2026-05-10 runtime owner follow-up:
  MIR resource/cleanup trace exports moved out of
  `pgy_runtime_lib_set_intent_trace_exports.c` into
  `pgy_runtime_lib_mir_trace_exports.c`, while `pgy_runtime_lib.c` still
  includes the owner so the single-runtime-source cache and LLVM runtime link
  model stay intact. This keeps the intent registry owner below the 560 LOC
  warning band without changing exported ABI. Gates used: targeted
  `gcc -fsyntax-only`, `test-inc-size-smoke`, `perf-contract-smoke`, and
  `build-source-inventory-smoke`.
- 2026-05-10 LLVM call-dispatch owner follow-up:
  callable-variable call lowering moved out of `llvm_expr_call_dispatch.c`
  into `llvm_expr_call_variable.c`. `llvm_expr_call_dispatch.c` is now below
  the 500 LOC band and the callable path has a named owner instead of living
  inside the top-level call dispatcher. Gate used: targeted `gcc
  -fsyntax-only`, `git diff --check`, `test-inc-size-smoke`, and
  `build-source-inventory-smoke`.
- 2026-05-10 growth-helper overflow follow-up:
  AIR/HIR/CFG/MIR/DIR/RIR/import/module-normalizer vector growth helpers now
  check `SIZE_MAX / 2` before doubling capacity instead of detecting overflow
  after wrapped arithmetic. This matches the DAG metadata growth policy and
  keeps compiler-owned dynamic arrays fail-closed on impossible sizes. Gate
  used: targeted `gcc -fsyntax-only` and `git diff --check`.
- 2026-05-10 semantic growth-helper follow-up:
  semantic module preload, live-slot collection, slot escape/access summaries,
  and symbol-table growth now use pre-doubling overflow checks. This removes
  another class of wrap-then-detect allocation paths from ownership/slot
  analysis. Gate used: targeted `gcc -fsyntax-only`, `git diff --check`, and
  `test-inc-size-smoke`.
- 2026-05-10 module-normalizer owner follow-up:
  shadow-name stack ownership moved from `module_normalizer_refs.c` to
  `module_normalizer_shadow.c`. The refs owner now focuses on AST reference
  rewriting, while shadow push/pop/contains/destroy has a named owner. Gate
  used: targeted `gcc -fsyntax-only` and `git diff --check`.
- 2026-05-10 LLVM MIR topology contract follow-up:
  `llvm_mir_validate_cleanup_contract(...)` now calls the central
  `mir_validate_emission_topology(...)` before running LLVM-specific cleanup
  checks. This aligns LLVM with the C backend contract path and keeps cleanup
  root/edge/source-of-truth validation owned by MIR instead of reimplemented
  differently in the backend. Gate used: targeted `gcc -fsyntax-only`,
  `git diff --check`, and `cfg-body-dataflow-test-smoke` source gate.
- 2026-05-10 runtime frontier / authority contract follow-up:
  LLVM intent authority failure reasons now emit the same `authority:%s`
  surface as the C backend contract, and `runtime_frontier_contract_smoke.sh`
  only treats generated-fixture emission as mandatory when `PGY_BIN` is
  explicitly supplied by Make/CI. Direct local source-contract runs no longer
  fail because a stale or foreign-ABI `bin/pgy.exe` happens to exist. Gates
  used: targeted `gcc -fsyntax-only`, `runtime-frontier-contract-smoke`,
  `perf-contract-smoke`, and `git diff --check`.
- 2026-05-10 runtime frontier panic vocabulary follow-up:
  bounded frontier overflow is now documented and smoke-gated as C `PGY_PANIC`
  plus LLVM `pgy_runtime_panic_internal_invariant_export`, not raw
  `abort()`. `runtime_frontier_contract_smoke.sh` explicitly rejects
  `llvm_lookup_or_create_function(ctx, "abort", ...)` in frontier/projection
  emitters. Gates used: `runtime-frontier-contract-smoke` and
  `runtime-frontier-policy-smoke`.
- 2026-05-10 runtime-none/raw-escape smoke portability follow-up:
  `raw_escape_contract_smoke.sh` and `runtime_none_contract_smoke.sh` now gate
  their source-level diagnostic/driver contracts before launching `pgy`. If the
  default local `bin/pgy(.exe)` is missing or belongs to a foreign ABI, direct
  shell runs skip only the executable probe; explicit `PGY_BIN` runs remain
  fail-closed for CI/Make. This keeps ABI ownership/runtime-none/raw-escape
  closure checks usable in the sandbox without weakening CI evidence.
- 2026-05-10 case-header size gate follow-up:
  AIR counter-only strict-evidence tests moved into
  `test_air_counter_strict_part_i.cases.h`, and the terminal CFG-owned MIR
  fallback regression moved into `test_mir_lowering_part_d.cases.h`. This keeps
  the new CFG/AIR source-of-truth regressions without violating the `src/tests`
  case-header size policy. Gates used: targeted `gcc -fsyntax-only`,
  `test-inc-size-smoke`, and `git diff --check`.
- 2026-05-10 MIR DCE source-location predicate follow-up:
  MIR DCE now consumes `mir_instruction_has_source_location(...)` from the MIR
  source-shape owner instead of reopening `inst->has_source_location` directly.
  The CFG/body smoke rejects raw source-location reads in `mir_dce.c`, keeping
  DCE on named MIR predicates while raw source fields remain owned by
  lifecycle/source-shape/debug display code. Gates used: targeted
  `gcc -fsyntax-only` and `cfg-body-dataflow-smoke`.
- 2026-05-10 MIR validator source-location predicate follow-up:
  MIR fact validation now also consumes `mir_instruction_has_source_location(...)`
  for source-shape checks instead of reopening the raw flag. This keeps the
  validator aligned with the same source-shape owner used by DCE and backend
  emission contracts. Gates used: targeted `gcc -fsyntax-only`,
  `cfg-body-dataflow-smoke`, and `test-inc-size-smoke`.
- 2026-05-10 MIR source-shape accessor follow-up:
  LLVM MIR block debug emission and MIR statement population now consume named
  MIR source-shape/source-location accessors instead of reopening
  `source_ast_type`, `has_source_location`, or source line fields directly.
  The CFG/body smoke rejects those raw backend/population reads so source
  shape stays owned by `mir_source_shape.c`. Gates used: targeted
  `gcc -fsyntax-only`, `cfg-body-dataflow-smoke`, and `perf-contract-smoke`.
- 2026-05-10 smoke runtime-cost follow-up:
  `build_source_inventory_smoke.sh` no longer launches one `git ls-files` and
  one `head|od|tr` pipeline per tracked example file. Deleted examples are
  computed once, and executable-artifact detection is now extension-based for
  tracked `tests/cases` and `examples` outputs. This keeps the inventory gate
  useful without turning the lean sprint loop into a per-file process storm.
  `perf_contract_smoke.sh` was also updated to follow the moved AIR
  counter-strict test split. Gates used: `build-source-inventory-smoke`,
  `perf-contract-smoke`, targeted `gcc -fsyntax-only`, and
  `cfg-body-dataflow-smoke`.
- 2026-05-10 build inventory duplicate-source follow-up:
  `ASYNC_SOURCES` is already folded into `RUNTIME_SOURCES`, so the build source
  inventory no longer prints the async list a second time. The inventory smoke
  now rejects duplicate source entries explicitly, preventing future Makefile
  source-list drift from being hidden by repeated object/source rows. Gate used:
  `build-source-inventory-smoke`.
- 2026-05-10 JS backend policy UTF recovery follow-up:
  `docs/23_js_backend_policy.md` was rewritten as a clean UTF-8 policy note
  after mojibake made the historical text unreadable. The recovered contract is
  intentionally narrow: direct `.pgy -> JS` is beta+1, WebGL dogfood goes
  through `Pergyra -> C --emit-c -> optional Emscripten/WebGL bridge`, and
  JS/WebGL pressure must not introduce core language surface.
- 2026-05-10 LLVM runtime owner follow-up:
  core/log/intent/authority runtime declarations moved from
  `llvm_runtime.c` into `llvm_runtime_core_builtin_decl.c`. The main runtime
  owner is now orchestration plus slot/Rc/array declarations instead of a
  single mixed declaration table, and the split follows the responsibility
  rule rather than a mechanical line-count cut. Gates used: targeted
  `gcc -fsyntax-only`, `build-source-inventory-smoke`, `test-inc-size-smoke`,
  `perf-contract-smoke`, and `git diff --check`.
- 2026-05-10 MIR declaration inventory mismatch follow-up:
  C and LLVM declaration lookup now fail closed when a MIR declaration header
  exists for a name but its `ast_type` does not match the requested declaration
  type. Before this, both backends could fall back to AST active inventory after
  observing a mismatched MIR header, which made declaration-header drift less
  visible. Gates used: targeted `gcc -fsyntax-only`, `perf-contract-smoke`,
  and `git diff --check`.
- 2026-05-10 LLVM hosted-method metadata closure follow-up:
  LLVM domain/role method forward and body emission now checks
  `llvm_hosted_method_view_missing_mir_metadata(...)` before iterating hosted
  methods. The C backend now applies the same guard to party/roster,
  relation/effect, zone/world, and generic class specialization method
  emission. MIR-enabled builds no longer silently skip hosted methods when
  declaration method metadata is absent and the AST compatibility source is
  intentionally blocked. MIR pin-region name generation failures also route
  through `llvm_set_mir_topology_invalid(...)` instead of generic LLVM errors,
  keeping MIR emission failures on the MIR diagnostic surface. Gates used:
  targeted `gcc -fsyntax-only`, `mir-declaration-inventory-smoke`, and
  `perf-contract-smoke`.
- 2026-05-10 hosted-method view parity follow-up:
  C/LLVM hosted-method views now preserve AST compatibility method counts even
  when a `MIRDeclHeader` exists, so MIR method metadata count drift is visible
  to `*_hosted_method_view_missing_mir_metadata(...)` instead of being hidden
  by a `NULL, 0` early return. The C backend also mirrors LLVM by accepting MIR
  method metadata only from host declaration headers, preventing non-host
  declaration rows with the same name from owning hosted-method lookup. LLVM
  pointer-self host classification now reads only host declaration headers, and
  C role MIR method lookup now requires `AST_ROLE_DECL` headers instead of
  trusting any matching declaration name. C host declaration classification is
  now centralized behind `transpiler_is_host_decl_type(...)`, so hosted-method
  views and nominal host lookup share one frozen host set. Gate used: targeted
  `gcc -fsyntax-only`, `mir-declaration-inventory-smoke`, and `git diff
  --check`.
- 2026-05-10 AIR backend non-impact smoke follow-up:
  `air_backend_nonimpact_smoke.sh` now mirrors the AIR JSON smoke behavior:
  generated backend-output comparison remains mandatory when Make/CI supplies
  `PGY_BIN`, but direct local source-contract runs skip cleanly when the only
  default compiler is a stale or foreign-ABI `bin/pgy.exe`. This keeps local
  debt scans usable without weakening CI. Gates used: `air-backend-nonimpact`
  direct smoke, `air-drift-smoke`, targeted `gcc -fsyntax-only`, and
  `git diff --check`.
- 2026-05-10 MIR fact owner follow-up:
  terminator provenance validation moved from `mir_fact_validate.c` into
  `mir_fact_terminator_validate.c`. `mir_fact_validate.c` now owns inventory,
  source-statement, ABI-layout, and surface-usage facts; the terminator owner
  owns branch/return provenance and source-branch emit facts. This keeps the
  last near-600 LOC production owner split by responsibility rather than by
  line count. Gates used: targeted `gcc -fsyntax-only`, `perf-contract-smoke`,
  `cfg-body-dataflow-smoke`, `build-source-inventory-smoke`,
  `test-inc-size-smoke`, and `git diff --check`.
- 2026-05-10 MIR emission-fact source-of-truth follow-up:
  `mir_validate_routine_emission_facts(...)` is now the central routine-level
  validator for source-statement inventory, source-compatible emission facts,
  intent facts, and terminator provenance. Both the C MIR emission contract
  and LLVM MIR cleanup/emission contract call it before backend-specific
  checks, so backends consume MIR facts instead of re-owning source-compatible
  body-safety validation. Gates used: targeted `gcc -fsyntax-only` and
  `cfg-body-dataflow-smoke`.
- 2026-05-10 with-slot Claim MIR fact follow-up:
  C and LLVM MIR emission no longer classify with-slot Claim paths by directly
  checking `source_ast_type == AST_WITH_STMT` in backend code. They now consume
  `mir_instruction_is_with_slot_claim(...)`, keeping the AST-shaped source
  compatibility rule in the MIR owner and leaving the backends to consume the
  named MIR fact. Gates used: targeted `gcc -fsyntax-only`,
  `cfg-body-dataflow-smoke`, `perf-contract-smoke`,
  `build-source-inventory-smoke`, `test-inc-size-smoke`, and
  `git diff --check`.
- 2026-05-11 CFG-owned wrapper/MIR ABI validation follow-up:
  `with` and `unsafe` wrappers are now treated as CFG-owned wrapper
  statements even when the containing block has no branch successors, so MIR
  population preserves their resource facts without resurrecting the wrapper
  as a fallback `STMT`. `mir_instruction_source_is_with_slot_claim(...)` also
  no longer requires `type_layout` to be present before classifying a Claim as
  a with-slot Claim; missing and invalid ABI layout facts are now validated by
  the fact validator instead of being hidden by the classifier. Gates used:
  `test-mir`, `cfg-body-dataflow-smoke`, `perf-contract-smoke`, and
  `test-inc-size-smoke`.
- 2026-05-11 AIR drift smoke inventory follow-up:
  `air-drift-smoke` now audits the counter-strict and RIR-propagation AIR
  regression owners (`test_air_counter_strict_part_i.cases.h` and
  `test_air_rir_propagation_part_j.cases.h`) instead of relying on stale
  `src/test_air.c` terms only. This keeps the smoke gate aligned with the
  active AIR test inventory. Gate used: `air-drift-smoke`.
- 2026-05-11 C backend domain transpile source-of-truth follow-up:
  relation/effect domain transpile regressions now emit through full
  `emit_program(ctx)` with the active MIR inventory instead of directly
  emitting raw top-level AST statements. The world/zone constructor regression
  also uses semantic-valid source (`Clone(battle)` for explicit world
  embedding and numeric-only `Player` construction) so the test no longer
  exercises synthetic fallback MIR for a program the real CLI rejects.
  `lower_program_to_mir_strict(...)` is now available for transpile cases that
  must prove they are on the real semantic/HIR/RIR/MIR path, while
  `lower_program_to_mir(...)` keeps the legacy synthetic fallback for the
  remaining inventory-only tests. The full
  domain async transpile owners now use the strict path, so the
  domain/runtime propagation C-backend regressions in those owners cannot pass
  through fallback MIR. Parsed-source program emission regressions in
  `test_transpile_program_part_a.cases.h` and
  `test_transpile_program_part_b.cases.h` also use the strict path; synthetic
  hand-built AST fixtures keep the fallback path intentionally. Gate used:
  `test-transpile`.
- 2026-05-11 C backend core transpile strict-path follow-up:
  parsed-source core transpile owners
  (`test_transpile_core_part_a.cases.h` and
  `test_transpile_core_part_b.cases.h`) now use
  `lower_program_to_mir_strict(...)`, keeping fallback MIR reserved for
  hand-built AST fixtures rather than normal parsed-source regressions. Gate
  used: `test-transpile`.
- 2026-05-11 C backend stdlib transpile strict-path follow-up:
  parsed-source stdlib transpile regressions now use
  `lower_program_to_mir_strict(...)`; synthetic hand-built AST fixtures in the
  same owner keep the compatibility fallback. Gate used: `test-transpile`.
- 2026-05-11 C backend parsed-source transpile fallback closure:
  all parsed-source transpile tests now route through
  `lower_program_to_mir_strict(...)`. Remaining uses of
  `lower_program_to_mir(...)` are limited to synthetic hand-built AST fixtures
  (`prog` / `make_program(...)`) that intentionally need declaration-inventory
  fallback coverage. `transpile-strict-source-test-smoke` now gates this split,
  is listed in the beta test-suite freeze, and is wired directly into the
  Linux/macOS/Windows CI targets so build-only Windows runs cannot skip the
  parsed-source source-of-truth check. The smoke also scans for
  `parse_program_from_string(...)` followed by fallback MIR lowering, not just
  the exact old helper-call spelling. Gates used: `test-transpile`,
  `transpile-strict-source-test-smoke`, and `beta-test-suite-freeze-test-smoke`.
- 2026-05-11 cross-platform MIR declaration inventory gate follow-up:
  `mir-declaration-inventory-test-smoke` is now wired directly into macOS and
  Windows CI in addition to Linux, keeping party/role/roster host lookup,
  active-inventory helper use, and declaration-side MIR-only compatibility
  seams source-gated on every beta support matrix lane. The gate is also part
  of the beta test-suite freeze list now, so CI wiring and beta contract cannot
  drift. Gates used:
  `mir-declaration-inventory-test-smoke`, `transpile-strict-source-test-smoke`,
  and `beta-test-suite-freeze-test-smoke`.
- 2026-05-11 LLVM host-name helper dedup follow-up:
  `llvm_current_host_decl_name(...)` now reuses `llvm_decl_node_name(...)` for
  host declarations instead of carrying a second host-name switch. This keeps
  party/role/roster/relation/effect/zone/world name support tied to the single
  declaration-name helper. `llvm_current_host_class_name(...)` now follows the
  same helper path, so self/field/projection host-name consumers cannot drift
  from active host classification. `llvm_decl.c` now consumes that same helper
  for implicit `self` parameter lowering instead of carrying a narrower local
  nominal-name switch. The MIR declaration inventory smoke gates helper reuse
  rather than duplicated switch spelling. Gate used:
  targeted `LLVM_ENABLED=1 build/codegen/llvm_inventory_decl_lookup.o`,
  `LLVM_ENABLED=1 build/codegen/llvm_domain_lookup.o`, and
  `LLVM_ENABLED=1 build/codegen/llvm_decl.o`, plus
  `mir-declaration-inventory-test-smoke`.
- 2026-05-20 DAG source-of-truth revalidation:
  resolver and materializer fallback seams remain at beta cap 0 after the
  latest CFG/body-flow and type-system owner cleanup. Current DAG counters are
  `graph-backed skips=2064`, `generic_param_nodes=102`,
  `dag_generic_contract_evidence=165`, `dag_ability_consumer_evidence=72`,
  `metadata_entries=3735`, `metadata_owned=261`, `metadata_hits=8771`,
  `metadata_dead_ends=0`, `metadata_entries=3735`,
  `metadata_owned=261`, and `metadata_hits=8771`; retired resolver and
  materializer compatibility mirrors are now quarantined or removed rather
  than treated as zero-only proof counters.
  Remaining DAG work is owner-local consumer simplification, not numeric
  fallback cleanup. Gates used:
  `type-resolution-resolver-inventory-test-smoke` and
  `type-resolution-dag-test-smoke`.
- 2026-05-11 cross-platform AIR drift gate follow-up:
  `air-drift-test-smoke` is now wired into macOS CI and the Windows native
  runnable lane, not Linux only. Cross-MinGW build-only Windows still keeps the
  shell/source and JSON AIR gates, while native Windows now runs the full AIR
  strict-evidence regression suite before `air-json-schema-test-smoke`. Gates
  used: `air-drift-test-smoke` and `beta-test-suite-freeze-test-smoke`.
- 2026-05-10 local-decl source-shape MIR fact follow-up:
  C MIR resource hook emission no longer checks `source_ast_type ==
  AST_LET_DECL` directly when deciding whether a Claim was already
  materialized by the source statement. It now consumes
  `mir_instruction_source_is_local_decl(...)`, keeping the source-compatible
  local-declaration shape in the MIR owner.
- 2026-05-10 source payload match MIR helper follow-up:
  C MIR block/resource statement emission now consumes
  `mir_instruction_source_matches_ast_type(...)` and
  `mir_instruction_source_matches_ast_node(...)` for source-compatible payload
  shape checks. This keeps AST-type equality as a MIR-owned compatibility fact
  instead of scattering raw `source_ast_type` equality in C backend helpers.
- 2026-05-10 defer source-shape MIR fact follow-up:
  LLVM MIR STMT emission now consumes `mir_instruction_source_is_defer_stmt(...)`
  before registering defer bodies, instead of directly comparing
  `source_ast_type` in the backend. The defer source-shape rule is now named
  in MIR next to local-decl and generic payload matching helpers.
- 2026-05-10 emission mapping source-shape MIR fact follow-up:
  C MIR emission mapping now consumes `mir_instruction_source_is_local_decl(...)`,
  `mir_instruction_source_is_local_destructure(...)`, and
  `mir_instruction_source_is_assignment(...)` when seeding SSA exit mappings
  for source-compatible STMT payloads. This removes another direct
  `source_ast_type` equality cluster from the backend contract owner.
- 2026-05-10 CFG-container source-shape MIR fact follow-up:
  LLVM MIR STMT residual emission now consumes
  `mir_instruction_source_is_cfg_container(...)` instead of reading
  `source_ast_type` directly. Backend debug printing may still display the raw
  source AST type, but CFG/residual emission policy now has a MIR-owned
  predicate.
- 2026-05-10 MIR source-shape owner follow-up:
  source-compatible MIR predicate helpers moved from `mir.c` into
  `mir_source_shape.c`. `mir.c` dropped back below the 600 LOC review gate, and
  source-shape compatibility now has a named owner instead of living in the
  general MIR lowering translation unit.
- 2026-05-10 CFG-owned control source-shape follow-up:
  `mir_instruction_source_is_cfg_owned_control(...)` now owns the compatibility
  rule for CFG-owned control statements that survived as fallback STMT
  instructions. CFG contract validation and MIR DCE consume that predicate
  instead of rebuilding `has_source_location` / `source_ast_type` / fallback AST
  checks locally. This keeps CFG-owned control rejection on the MIR
  source-shape owner rather than on ad-hoc consumer logic.
- 2026-05-10 MIR DCE source-shape follow-up:
  MIR DCE now consumes
  `mir_instruction_source_stmt_has_side_effect_hint(...)` for source-shaped
  STMT side-effect classification instead of owning a local
  `source_ast_type` switch. The source-location-less compatibility AST path now
  also consumes `mir_source_ast_stmt_has_side_effect_hint(...)`, so DCE no
  longer owns the call-purity whitelist or statement side-effect switch. The
  AST/type hint policy is centralized in `mir_source_shape.c`. Gates used:
  targeted `gcc -fsyntax-only`, `cfg-body-dataflow-smoke`,
  `perf-contract-smoke`, and `git diff --check`.
- 2026-05-10 source-compatible branch fact follow-up:
  branch-shape/source-payload matching moved into MIR helpers
  `mir_instruction_branch_requires_source_emit(...)` and
  `mir_instruction_source_branch_payload_matches_shape(...)`. MIR validation
  and C/LLVM emission contracts now share the same MIR-owned rule instead of
  duplicating match/select source-shape checks in backend contract code. Gates
  used: targeted `gcc -fsyntax-only`, `cfg-body-dataflow-smoke`, and
  `perf-contract-smoke`.
- 2026-05-10 branch source-emit consumer follow-up:
  C/LLVM branch condition emission and the C MIR emission contract now consume
  `mir_instruction_branch_requires_source_emit(...)` instead of reading
  `requires_source_branch_emit` directly. The raw flag remains MIR inventory,
  but backend consumers now depend on the MIR-owned branch-shape predicate.
- 2026-05-10 source-compatible DEF fact follow-up:
  source-statement/local-decl/channel-receive/select-receive emission predicate
  composition moved into MIR helpers:
  `mir_instruction_uses_source_statement_emit(...)`,
  `mir_instruction_uses_source_local_decl_emit(...)`,
  `mir_instruction_uses_channel_receive_statement_emit(...)`, and
  `mir_instruction_uses_select_receive_statement_emit(...)`. C/LLVM backend
  helpers now wrap these MIR facts instead of rebuilding the flag lattice
  locally. The pending-use materializer also consumes the local-decl helper
  instead of rechecking source flags plus `AST_LET_DECL` in codegen, and C
  MIR block/assignment emission no longer reads the `requires_source_*` flags
  directly. AIR select-receive evidence counting now consumes the same MIR
  helper instead of reading the raw select-receive flag. Gates used: targeted
  `gcc -fsyntax-only`, `cfg-body-dataflow-smoke`, `air-drift-smoke`,
  `perf-contract-smoke`, and `git diff --check`.
- 2026-05-10 source payload MIR fact follow-up:
  LLVM MIR block emission no longer composes `inst->ast != NULL` with
  `has_source_location` locally when deciding whether a source-compatible
  payload exists. It now consumes `mir_instruction_has_source_payload(...)`
  from `mir_source_shape.c`, keeping source-payload shape ownership in MIR and
  leaving backend raw source reads only for actual payload emission/debug
  display. Gates used: targeted `gcc -fsyntax-only`,
  `cfg-body-dataflow-smoke`, `perf-contract-smoke`, and `git diff --check`.
- 2026-05-10 block source-mapping MIR fact follow-up:
  AIR terminator fallback evidence and C MIR block mapping comments now consume
  `mir_block_has_hir_source_mapping(...)`,
  `mir_block_has_source_location(...)`, and the corresponding source-id/line
  accessors from `mir_source_shape.c`. This keeps block source mapping as a
  MIR-owned compatibility fact instead of letting AIR/codegen reopen raw block
  source fields for policy or display decisions. Gates used: targeted
  `gcc -fsyntax-only`, `cfg-body-dataflow-smoke`, and `air-drift-smoke`.
- 2026-05-10 MIR fact validator source-shape follow-up:
  `mir_fact_validate.c` now consumes the MIR source-shape helpers for local
  declaration, assignment, defer, with-slot Claim, and AST-call matching checks
  instead of rebuilding raw `source_ast_type` comparisons inline. The validator
  remains the owner of the fact rules, but source-shape classification is now
  shared with the backend/AIR consumers through the same named predicates.
  Gates used: targeted `gcc -fsyntax-only`, `cfg-body-dataflow-smoke`, and
  `mir-declaration-inventory-smoke`.
- 2026-05-10 MIR intent source-shape follow-up:
  intent fact validation now consumes
  `mir_instruction_source_is_intent_step(...)` instead of directly reopening
  `has_source_location` plus `source_ast_type == AST_INTENT_STEP`. Intent-step
  anchoring remains a MIR validation rule, but the AST-shaped source predicate
  is centralized in `mir_source_shape.c`.
- 2026-05-10 AIR strict runtime evidence follow-up:
  strict AIR now treats global runtime observability schema evidence and
  runtime frontier policy evidence as required verifier inputs, not merely
  optional evidence nodes that are validated if present. Missing
  `AIR_EVIDENCE_OBSERVABILITY_SCHEMA` or
  `AIR_EVIDENCE_RUNTIME_FRONTIER_POLICY` now produces drift before
  abstraction-boundary verification can claim runtime/trace ABI coverage.
  Gates used: targeted `gcc -fsyntax-only`, `air-drift-smoke`, and
  `air-json-schema-smoke`.
- 2026-05-10 AIR global evidence validator coverage follow-up:
  `air_validate_global_evidence_node(...)` now rejects any global
  `AIREvidenceKind` that has no explicit global validator. This prevents a new
  global evidence kind from being classified as global and then passing through
  the individual validator chain as a sequence of no-op checks. `air-drift`
  now gates the validator coverage hook. Gates used: targeted
  `gcc -fsyntax-only`, `air-drift-smoke`, and `git diff --check`.
- 2026-05-10 AIR global evidence source-of-truth follow-up:
  strict AIR now checks global evidence through the `AIREvidenceNode`
  inventory, not through summary counters alone. The counters remain dump/stat
  fields, but MIR terminator, observability schema, runtime frontier policy,
  and RIR propagation strictness now consume `air_global_has_evidence_kind(...)`
  / `air_global_evidence_fact_count(...)`. Counter-only fixtures are rejected
  by regression tests so summary fields cannot become a second evidence source
  of truth. Gates used: targeted `gcc -fsyntax-only`, `air-drift-smoke`, and
  `air-json-schema-smoke`; `test-air` could not run in this local shell because
  Git Bash lacks `make`, native `mingw32-make` runs Unix shell recipes under
  `cmd`, and WSL has no installed distribution.
- 2026-05-10 DAG type-ref seam follow-ups:
  the earlier intent, transfer, boundary/type-contract, annotation-only,
  constructor/generic-boundary, host/call-contract, and expression-contract
  materializing-seam slices are superseded by the 2026-05-11 closure above.
  Current policy is metadata-only owner seams plus local diagnostics; the old
  `semantic_type_resolution_lookup_type_ref_or_materialize(...)` helper is
  absent under `src/semantic`, and annotation-only / nullable reads are gated
  at zero.
- 2026-05-10 domain slot type-ref DAG seam follow-up:
  domain slot/shared type references now enter the central
  metadata type-ref seam through domain slot/shared/named owner APIs instead
  of annotation-only lookup or the retired broad `domain_resolve_type_ref(...)`
  API. This puts zone authority subject-slot matching and
  relation/effect/zone/world domain slot validation on the same DAG metadata
  path as intent type refs.
  Gates used: targeted `gcc -fsyntax-only`; full semantic DAG execution still
  requires `SEMANTIC_TEST_BIN` in this local shell.
- 2026-05-10 zone authority slot-type DAG seam follow-up:
  zone authority validation no longer owns a local annotation-only subject-slot
  type resolver. It now consumes `domain_lookup_slot_type_metadata(...)`, so authority
  subject-slot matching shares the domain DAG materialization path.
- 2026-05-10 ability contract DAG seam follow-up:
  ability declaration signatures, `fields` requirements, and ability
  where-bound validation now consume metadata-only owner facts instead of
  annotation-only lookup. Nominal/overlay, world/action/module, and
  boundary/projection consumers have likewise converged to metadata-only
  owners. The old classified helper-user caps are superseded by the current
  `type-ref helper refs=0` gate.
- 2026-05-10 annotation-only DAG read guard:
  `type_resolution_resolver_inventory_smoke.sh` now also caps direct
  annotation-or-unknown users at zero regardless of line wrapping. New
  declaration, contract, boundary, projection, or authority paths must use
  metadata-first type-ref helpers or update the audit with an explicit
  source-of-truth justification. Gate used:
  `type-resolution-resolver-inventory-smoke`.

External review risk intake, 2026-05-08:

- Build/toolchain portability is a beta trust item, not a language feature:
  Unix-style `make` remains the source of truth, but Windows users need an
  explicit MSYS2/MinGW or WSL path. Add a preflight target that checks `gcc`,
  `bash`, `make`/`mingw32-make`, optional `llvm-config`, and optional assembler
  tools before compiling. Failure should be a clear diagnostic, not a partial
  build error. Support matrix stays Linux C+LLVM, Windows C-first with LLVM
  only when executable toolchain evidence exists.
- Release/debug hygiene needs a gate:
  `PGY_DEBUG_LLVM_DETAIL`, `PGY_DEBUG_LLVM_STAGE`, and similar developer trace
  flags must be off by default in release/profiled builds. Add a smoke that
  rejects unconditional debug tracing in hot production code paths and documents
  the supported environment-variable debug surface.
- Memory/string safety audit remains open:
  scan `memcpy`, `strncpy`, `strncat`, manual buffer writes, and fixed-size
  formatting paths for explicit capacity proofs. This is not a claim that every
  use is unsafe; it is a required beta audit bucket because compiler/runtime C
  code must make bounds reasoning visible.
- MIR-missing diagnostics are intentional hard gates:
  messages such as `MIR-only LLVM path missing routine` are acceptable only as
  structured backend errors proving no silent fallback occurred. They must stay
  smoke-gated, use actionable `Reason:` / `Fix:` text, and never represent
  successful partial code generation.
- Security/runtime portability needs narrower claims:
  Slot/SecureSlot token, HMAC/AES, generation, and authority checks must be
  described as implemented runtime validation plus targeted smoke coverage, not
  as a fully audited cryptographic platform. Add Linux/Windows smoke coverage
  for secure-slot invalid token, released slot, generation mismatch, and
  authority rejection; macOS remains support-matrix work until CI evidence is
  present.
- Documentation/implementation drift must be treated as a failing gate:
  README/status/checklist wording must distinguish stable beta surface,
  explicit reject, experimental, and beta-out-of-scope. Quantum/QubitSlot stays
  experimental/v2; WASM/WebGL stays module/dogfood bridge, not core language
  surface; debugger remains source-level until DWARF/CodeView work lands.
- Ownership failure coverage remains a beta blocker:
  anchored own/ref, Slot/Pin cleanup, channel/world transfer, and authority
  boundary failures need regression coverage for both static rejection and
  runtime hard-fail/queryable failure cases. Do not market this as a Rust
  borrow checker; it is layered static boundary verification plus runtime
  handle validation.
- Hardened C domain nominal diagnostic surface formatting:
  ability method parameters, role override parameters, party shared fields, and
  roster shared fields now route through a checked formatter instead of
  accepting truncated `snprintf` output. Gate:
  `memory-string-safety-test-smoke`.
- Hardened C relation/effect diagnostic surface formatting:
  relation/effect slots and shared fields now reject overlong diagnostic
  surfaces instead of passing clipped strings into type-requirement errors.
  Gate: `memory-string-safety-test-smoke`.
- Hardened C class generated-name and diagnostic formatting:
  class field/method-parameter type diagnostics and MIR-backed class method
  emitted names now reject overlong generated strings instead of using clipped
  stack buffers. Gate: `memory-string-safety-test-smoke`.
- Hardened C stdlib collection type-buffer copies:
  HashMap/List/Set/Queue alias resolution and inner-type extraction now check
  fixed buffer capacity before copying rendered type names, so collection
  metadata cannot silently continue with a truncated concrete type. Gate:
  `memory-string-safety-test-smoke`.
- Hardened C function lowering state string handling:
  function return-type tracking and parameter diagnostic surfaces now use
  checked helpers, rejecting overlong names before body lowering can consume a
  truncated `current_return_type`. Gate: `memory-string-safety-test-smoke`.
- Hardened C MIR emit-state return-type snapshots:
  capture/restore/set of `current_return_type` now use a checked copy helper
  and report a backend error instead of clipping emit-state type facts. Gate:
  `memory-string-safety-test-smoke`.
- Hardened C zone diagnostic surface formatting:
  zone slots and shared fields now reject overlong diagnostic surfaces before
  type requirement checks, matching relation/effect/domain nominal policy.
  Gate: `memory-string-safety-test-smoke`.
- Hardened C intent binding diagnostic surface formatting:
  intent participant/value forward-declaration type diagnostics now reject
  overlong surface strings before binding emission, keeping intent contract
  errors from using clipped aliases or intent names. Gate:
  `memory-string-safety-test-smoke`.
- Hardened C stdlib unary constructed type-buffer copies:
  Array/Slice/Channel alias resolution and inner-type extraction now check
  capacity before copying rendered type names, so stdlib lowering cannot
  consume truncated concrete type metadata. Gate:
  `memory-string-safety-test-smoke`.
- Hardened C enum method generated-name and diagnostic formatting:
  MIR-backed enum method emitted names and enum method parameter diagnostics now
  reject overlong generated strings instead of consuming clipped stack buffers.
  Gate: `memory-string-safety-test-smoke`.
- Hardened C pin-block generated address formatting:
  pin block slot/token address fragments now check `&name` formatting before
  emission and report a backend error instead of generating clipped C code.
  Gate: `memory-string-safety-test-smoke`.
- Hardened C declaration lookup cache names:
  active-inventory lookup cache keys now use a checked store helper and skip
  caching overlong names instead of comparing against truncated cache keys.
  Gate: `memory-string-safety-test-smoke`.
- Hardened C intent prologue diagnostic surface formatting:
  intent participant/value signature emission now rejects overlong diagnostic
  surfaces before type lowering, matching intent forward-declaration policy.
  Gate: `memory-string-safety-test-smoke`.
- Hardened C let-slot constructed type formatting:
  View/Move lowering now checks temporary `Slot<T>`/`SecureSlot<T>` type names
  before passing them to C type mapping, instead of allowing truncated
  constructed type metadata. Gate: `memory-string-safety-test-smoke`.
- Hardened C event builtin dynamic formatting:
  event invocation string allocation now verifies the second `snprintf` result
  matches the measured length, freeing the buffer on mismatch. Gate:
  `memory-string-safety-test-smoke`.
- Hardened C parallel/async capture diagnostic formatting:
  capture type diagnostics now reject overlong capture names instead of using
  precision-truncated surface strings. Gate:
  `memory-string-safety-test-smoke`.
- Hardened C specialization registry names:
  Result, collection, and tuple specialization cache entries now use checked
  assembly/copies and raise a backend error on overlong generated names instead
  of storing truncated registry keys. Gate: `memory-string-safety-test-smoke`.
- Hardened C generic class diagnostic surface formatting:
  generic class field and fallback method-parameter type diagnostics now reject
  overlong specialization/member surfaces instead of passing clipped names to
  C type requirement checks. Gate: `memory-string-safety-test-smoke`.
- Hardened LLVM API error-message formatting:
  context, verifier, and object-emission errors now use arena-backed formatted
  result helpers instead of fixed 1024-byte stack buffers, preserving full
  diagnostic text at the public backend API boundary. Gate:
  `memory-string-safety-test-smoke`.
- Hardened semantic SecureSlot token-name materialization:
  implicit paired token names now go through a checked formatter shared by
  let-claim, annotated let, function parameter, and member-call fallback paths,
  so overlong slot names cannot silently truncate the slot/token capability
  invariant. Gate: `memory-string-safety-test-smoke`.
- Hardened AIR verifier drift/provenance formatting:
  strict evidence drift messages, invariant errors, authority participant
  lists, and boundary provenance strings now use owned dynamic formatting
  instead of fixed stack buffers. This keeps AIR's verification-layer
  diagnostic surface from clipping CFG/MIR/DAG/effect evidence context. Gate:
  `memory-string-safety-test-smoke`.
- Hardened MIR claim type-name rendering:
  MIR claim ABI type names now build generic type strings with owned dynamic
  append instead of a fixed 256-byte buffer, and MIR formatted-string helpers
  verify the second `vsnprintf` length before returning. This prevents
  truncated `Slot<T>` / `Channel<T>` / nested generic names from becoming ABI
  lookup facts. Gate: `memory-string-safety-test-smoke`.
- Hardened MIR ABI generic suffix extraction:
  `mir_abi_lookup(...)` now extracts generic inner suffixes and generated
  release/runtime lookup names into owned exact strings instead of fixed
  64/128-byte buffers, so runtime-function lookup cannot accidentally use a
  truncated generic payload suffix or helper name. Gate:
  `memory-string-safety-test-smoke`.
- Hardened MIR shared formatted-string allocation:
  `mir_strdup_fmt(...)` now verifies the second `vsnprintf` result before
  returning owned strings, aligning MIR error/name formatting with the AIR
  formatting contract. Gate: `memory-string-safety-test-smoke`.
- Hardened MIR dump label/source-location formatting:
  `mir_dump(...)` now formats block labels and source-location strings through
  `mir_strdup_fmt(...)` instead of fixed stack buffers, so CFG dump evidence
  cannot clip long routine names while debugging body-safety facts. Gate:
  `memory-string-safety-test-smoke`.
- Hardened MIR validation formatted-string clones:
  declaration-header validation, fact validation, intent-fact diagnostics, and
  global MIR validation now verify their second `vsnprintf` result before
  returning owned diagnostic strings. Gate: `memory-string-safety-test-smoke`.
- Hardened MIR SSA versioned-name parsing:
  SSA use-edge population now parses versioned result names into owned exact
  base strings instead of a fixed 128-byte buffer, so long local names cannot
  silently skip current-version updates during CFG/body dataflow. Gate:
  `memory-string-safety-test-smoke`.
- Hardened common owned printf helper:
  `pergyra_strdup_vprintf(...)` now verifies the second `vsnprintf` result
  before returning owned strings, so users of the shared compatibility helper
  inherit the same no-clipped-owned-string contract as AIR and MIR. Gate:
  `memory-string-safety-test-smoke`.

Progress log, 2026-05-08:

- Added a runtime frontier publish-order contract:
  `pgy_frontier_policy.h` now names the write-value, write-epoch,
  write-cause, ready, and clear-dirty phases and rejects invalid or reversed
  phase order. The AIR runtime frontier policy fact count was raised with the
  contract, and `runtime-frontier-policy-test-smoke` compiles and executes the
  phase-order probe so the scheduler cannot silently regress to clearing dirty
  state before publishing ready state.
- Tightened runtime frontier AIR evidence:
  `PGY_FRONTIER_POLICY_FACT_COUNT` now derives from 9 pass-limit facts plus 5
  bounded-overflow reason facts. AIR JSON therefore publishes the same frontier
  policy surface that C/LLVM consume from `pgy_frontier_policy.h`, including
  separate sub-counts for pass-limit arithmetic and overflow-reason policy.
- Split AST domain read-only accessors out of the domain constructor owner:
  `ast_domain_constructors.c` now stays constructor-focused, while
  `ast_domain_accessors.c` owns ability/role/roster/world/relation/effect
  accessors and `ast_zone_accessors.c` owns zone accessors. This closes the
  remaining production owner above the 600 LOC gate without introducing
  implementation headers.
- Matched C MIR emission pin-region validation to LLVM/MIR:
  the C emission contract now rejects a reachable pin block that has no cleanup
  successor before checking the pin-unpin cleanup fact. This keeps both
  backends consuming the same MIR cleanup topology contract.
- Hardened the DAG metadata index owner:
  `type_checker_resolution_metadata_index.c` now validates the power-of-two
  open-addressing capacity invariant before insert/lookup/rebuild paths. The
  index remains a private acceleration cache over DAG metadata, not a second
  type-resolution source of truth.
- Lifted HashMap key codegen policy to a sorted lookup table:
  `codegen_hashmap_key_policy.c` now uses the same bsearch-backed policy shape
  as Slot/Pin call classification for the beta-stable key subset
  (`Bool`, `Int`, `Long`, `String`). `perf-contract-test-smoke` gates both the
  lookup seam and sorted table order so future collection additions do not
  reintroduce local strcmp chains.
- Hardened MIR resource runtime-name formatting:
  slot runtime operation selection now uses a sorted bsearch table, and
  `transpiler_format_slot_runtime_fn(...)` returns failure on `snprintf`
  truncation instead of treating a clipped runtime symbol as a valid codegen
  result. Gates: `perf-contract-test-smoke`,
  `memory-string-safety-test-smoke`.
- Hardened LLVM channel runtime-name formatting:
  channel send/receive expression emit now rejects overlong generated runtime
  helper names instead of looking up a truncated `pgy_channel_*` symbol.
  Gate: `memory-string-safety-test-smoke`.
- Hardened LLVM task/channel runtime-name formatting:
  task/channel builtins (`ChannelClose`, `TrySend`, timeout send/receive,
  channel state queries) now share bounded runtime-name formatters and reject
  truncation before runtime function lookup. Gate:
  `memory-string-safety-test-smoke`.
- Hardened LLVM parallel/async/select generated names:
  `llvm_stmt_parallel_async.c` now checks generated parallel context/task
  wrapper names, async wrapper names, select round-robin globals, and select
  channel runtime lookup names before adding LLVM symbols or looking up

- Hardened LLVM slot/device runtime-name formatting:
  core Slot/SecureSlot and DeviceSlot builtin emit now rejects overlong

- Hardened LLVM array runtime-name formatting:
  ArrayPush/ArraySet/ArrayPop helper names now go through a bounded formatter

- Hardened LLVM member slot-method runtime-name formatting:

- Hardened C MIR pin address/name formatting:

- Hardened C backend constructed type-name formatting:
  `transpiler_type_mapping.c` now routes generated collection, Slot/Pin,
  channel, Rc/Weak, Result, and Option C type names through a bounded join
  helper and returns `Unknown` instead of emitting truncated generated type
  names. Gate: `memory-string-safety-test-smoke`.
- Hardened C backend nominal host lookup cache keys:
  `transpiler_decl_host_lookup.c` now stores nominal host/method cache keys
  only when they fit exactly in the fixed cache buffers; overlong names still
  return the lookup result but do not poison future cache comparisons with
  truncated keys. Gate: `memory-string-safety-test-smoke`.
- Hardened LLVM Result layout-name formatting:
  `llvm_type.c` now checks `Result<T,E>` suffix joins, generated
